public_rationale: There are documented examples of generous allowances and later restrictions. They do not establish the claimed prevalence or cost multiple. API-equivalent value is not provider cost, and heavy-user cases do not describe the typical subscriber. Anthropic's reported estimate that new limits would affect fewer than 5% of subscribers further limits that inference, without disproving subsidies elsewhere.
limitations: Private providers rarely disclose subscription-level delivery costs.
The available evidence supports examples, not a market-wide estimate.
Different meanings of subscription population and token value could change a future assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast majority of AI subscriptions are heavily subsidized, letting users burn several dollars' worth of tokens per subscription dollar while companies absorb the cost to acquire them, only to rugpull them in the following months or years as they try to rein in costs.

statement.excerpt: the vast majority of AI subscriptions are heavily subsidized, letting users burn several dollars’ worth of tokens for every dollar worth of subscription and eating the costs to get them through the door, only to rugpull them the months or years to follow as the company in question tries to pull costs in.

from_speaker: the vast majority of AI subscriptions
several dollars’ worth of tokens for every dollar worth of subscription
eating the costs to get them through the door
rugpull them the months or years to follow
our_interpretation: Read this as an asserted market-wide business pattern, including existing examples of later retrenchment, rather than a forecast about a specified future cohort.
The plain reading requires a large majority of paid AI subscriptions, not merely a few unusually heavy users.
Because the claim says providers absorb costs, subsidy requires delivery costs exceeding associated receipts. API retail value alone does not establish provider cost.
Read 'rugpull' as materially worse prices or usage allowances introduced to contain costs, without importing an allegation of fraud.
Use Q3 2026 as the latest completed quarter for current unit economics. Include the historical pattern from June 2025, which the surrounding text identifies as its beginning.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence establishes widespread delivery costs several times subscription receipts, an acquisition or retention rationale, and subsequent cost-driven pricing or allowance reductions across a large majority of the relevant subscriptions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that most subscriptions cover delivery costs, or that the claimed subsidy-and-retrenchment pattern is confined to a minority.
